transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—I'm Dr. [Name]. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Dr. [Name]. Um, thank you for seeing me. I hope I'm not taking up time from people who need it more, but... well, I guess I'm just having a little trouble keeping on top of things lately? 

It's probably just normal stress from graduating and trying to figure out life, but I've been, um, letting a few things slip. Just silly things, really, but they're starting to pile up. Like, I'll forget to pay a bill until the last minute, or I'll mean to reply to an email about a job interview and then completely lose track of it. And I've missed a couple of appointments recently, which is so embarrassing. I really hate being that person who flakes on errands or commitments, you know? I'm trying really hard to be organized, but it feels like I'm messing up some real opportunities. Does that make sense? I just want to make sure I'm not overreacting.
Have you always had trouble staying organized and keeping track of things since childhood, or is this something new that started around the time you graduated?

Um... well, to be completely honest, I guess it's not entirely new? I mean, I don't want to make a big deal out of it, because I know a lot of kids are a little scattered, right? 

But... yeah, if I think back to even elementary school, my teachers would always write on my report cards that I was a bright student—which was really nice of them!—but they'd usually add these little notes. Like, that I was constantly losing my worksheets, or that my desk was so messy I could never find my assignments when it was time to hand them in. I also had a bad habit of rushing through directions, and... um, talking out of turn in class. I always felt so awful about it because I really, really wanted to be a good student and not cause trouble for the teachers. 

So I guess it has been around for a while, even if it feels more overwhelming now. Is that the kind of thing you're asking about? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.

Aside from feeling bad about missing things, do you find yourself worrying excessively about a lot of different things—like your health, finances, or relationships—on most days, even when there's no clear reason to?

Oh, um... no, I don't think so. I mean, I definitely feel terrible when I let people down or, you know, forget to pay a bill, like I was saying. Because I really hate causing problems for anyone. But it's usually tied to something I actually messed up on. 

I don't really just sit around worrying about my health or relationships out of nowhere. I try to be a pretty positive person most of the time! I just... I just get stressed when I drop the ball and know I've disappointed someone. Is that... does that make sense? I hope I'm answering what you're looking for.

These symptoms have persisted into adulthood, now manifesting as missed bills, unanswered emails, and missed appointments, causing functional impairment in occupational/life domains (e.g., jeopardizing job opportunities).
